Definition: to breathe after, i.e. to love (sensually)
BiblicalUsage: Agab is lust — inordinate, sensual affection — and it appears only in the prophets' picture of unfaithful Israel. Jerusalem 'doted' on her lovers, the Assyrians and the Babylonians, chasing foreign powers and foreign gods the way a faithless wife chases other men. Jeremiah says her lovers will despise her, and Ezekiel says the very nations she doted on would be the ones to judge her.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word is a warning about misplaced love. The heart that chases what God forbids always ends despised by what it chased, and the only safe affection is the one fixed on the Lord who never betrays His people.
